newsitem.title: INDIA: INDIAN SUGAR UP ON FESTIVAL DEMAND, LOWER SUPPLY.
newsitem.headline: INDIAN SUGAR UP ON FESTIVAL DEMAND, LOWER SUPPLY.

text.p: Indian sugar ended Thursday up on increased demand ahead of the festival season and limited supply, dealers said.
In ready delivery, sugar S-30 rose 5 rupees to 1,495/1,520 rupees per quintal while sugar M-30 moved up by 5/8 rupees to 1,525/1,550 rupees per quintal.
"Absence of fresh offerings by millers kept arrivals at a low ebb," one dealer said.
"Local millers have already sold out their allotted quantity of free sale sugar for the first half of the current month; in turn sugar mill delivery also remained untraded today," he said.
Free sale quota for August is 750,000 tonnes, unchanged from last month. It was 800,000 tonnes in June.
The Bombay sugar market is closed on Friday for Independence Day and on Monday for a local festival.
